text:
Maya: FYI — noticed p99 for shared-gpu pool-c climbed from ~120ms to ~220ms over a 5m window around 14:03 UTC. Spike correlates with a weird pattern in KV cache hit rate dropping to ~30%.
Sam: Can you paste the shorttrace/flamegraph link?
Maya: https://perf.internal/runs/194512 — flamegraph shows repeated kernel switches every ~200ms, plus lots of small requests with <32 tokens. KV shows repeated invalidations.
Priya: Did autoscaler kick or any scheduling churn? k8s events are quiet. No node resizes in that window.
Kendrick: Uploading the tail logs: ```
[2026-03-18T14:02:59Z] tenant=acme req_id=... latency=18ms kernel=fp16_q8 kv_hit=false
[2026-03-18T14:03:00Z] tenant=acme req_id=... latency=190ms kernel=fp16_q4 kv_hit=false
[2026-03-18T14:03:01Z] tenant=other req_id=... latency=20ms kernel=fp16_q8 kv_hit=true
```
Maya: Notice tenant=acme doing rapid alternating short/long sequences. Hypothesis: their client pattern pins model kernel to q4 variant because of a long request, then subsequent short requests suffer kernel swap overhead + cold KV cache.
Sam: That would explain kernel churn + KV thrash. Do we have per-tenant kernel pinning TTLs?
Priya: Current behavior: we pin last-used kernel for 60s when the sequence contains a request >512 tokens to avoid constant reprovisioning. But we didn’t account for mixed short tail traffic inside that window.
Ella: If pin TTL is too long, multi-tenant bursts can cause unfairness. Suggestation: make TTL adaptive based on per-tenant short-request ratio.
Kendrick: Also saw batching heuristics collapse — the batcher slowed to flush immediately when kernel swap detected, so throughput dropped. Batcher logs: `batcher.flush_reason=kernel_switch` repeated.
Maya: Proposed mitigation for prod: 1) temporarily reduce kernel-pin TTL from 60s -> 8s for shared pools C. 2) Add early KV prefetch for tenants with high short-request rate. 3) Rate-limit very high short-request QPS per-tenant (soft throttle). Anyone opposed?
Sam: +1 for TTL change as quick rollbackable knob. We should also add a perf test that replays mixed short/long sequence to verify.
Priya: I'll open a PR to make TTL adaptive and add a feature flag to flip on the 8s TTL for pool-c. I'll also add a regression test in perf-replay harness.
Maya: Kendrick, can you push an emergency ff (feature-flag) to reduce TTL and watch p99?
Kendrick: On it. Pushing flag now. infra-bot: create incident ticket and annotate with rollout.
infra-bot: Incident INC-20260318-77 created for shared-gpu pool-c p99 spike. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-20260318-77
Kendrick: Flag is live in prod for pool-c. Early telemetry shows p99 back down to ~130ms (still slightly above baseline). KV hit rate climbing from 30% -> 62%.
Maya: Good. Next steps: Priya to wire adaptive TTL + perf replay, Sam to add telemetry for kernel-switch-induced flush reasons, Ella to propose per-tenant short-request QPS soft-limits for shared pools. We'll re-evaluate tomorrow in 09:30 sync.
Ella: I'll draft the soft-limit proposal and simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.
Sam: Also let's add a lightweight kernel-switch metric per-tenant so we can alert earlier if a tenant triggers repeated switches.
Maya: Thanks team. I'll annotate the incident with what we rolled and link to the flamegraph.
Priya: PR opened: `runtime: adaptive-kernel-ttl flag` -> https://git.internal/r/12345. Contains perf-replay script and unit tests.
Maya: Closing loop — mark this thread resolved once p99 stable for 2h post-change.
